To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
optogenetic activation of the TrkA receptor in the absence of its ligand, nerve growth factor, reveals a novel role for TrkA in PC12 cell neuronal differentiation.

we used optogenetics to delineate the contributions of TrkA receptor tyrosine phosphorylation sites to nerve growth factor induced extracellular signal regulated kinases activation and PC12 cell differentiation.

we have developed an optogenetics system to study TrkA mediated signaling in PC12 cells and have shown that Y490 and 785 each contributes to differentiation through extracellular signal regulated protein kinases in an additive manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of optogenetic systems for studying receptor mediated signaling.
the mechanisms of cell fate specification and differentiation.
the mechanisms of cell differentiation and the development of new technologies for the mechanistic analysis of signaling networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
optogenetic TrKA activation in the absence of NGF is sufficient to induce PC12 cell differentiation.
the optogenetic approach described in this paper is a useful tool to dissect signaling mechanisms and to study the role of specific signaling pathways in cellular differentiation.
Y490 and/or Y785 of TrkA are required for nerve growth factor-induced differentiation in PC12 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel optogenetic method to study TrkA signaling and found that Y490 and 785 both contribute to differentiation in PC12 cells in an additive manner.
we have used optogenetics to delineate the signaling outcomes of two tyrosine residues on the TrkA receptor in PC12 cell neurite outgrowth.
we have developed a novel approach for studying signaling pathways in PC12 cells and other systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extracellular signal-regulated kinase pathway is activated in an additive manner through both TrkA Y490 and Y795 phosphorylation sites.
optogenetic activation of a receptor tyrosine kinase is a useful tool to delineate receptor tyrosine kinases subcircuits.
